definitions.explanation: A hand-cranked friction machine that produces static electricity, brought to Japan by the Dutch in the eighteenth century. {平賀源内|ひらがげんない} famously repaired and rebuilt one in 1776, and it became a symbol of Edo-period curiosity about Western science.

notes:
From Dutch elektriciteit (electricity). The word survives today mainly in history lessons and in talk about ⟦{平賀源内|ひらがげんない}→平賀源内：33900_hiragagennai⟧; the modern word for electricity is ⟦{電気|でんき}→電気：09780_denki⟧.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The elekiter was shown off as a curiosity and even used as a supposed medical treatment, giving mild shocks to patients. One of {源内|げんない}'s machines survives and is designated an Important Cultural Property.
